relevance_note: Case report of a woman and her mother with a LAMP2 variant: "A nonsense mutation in the LAMP2 gene (c.123C>A; p.Cys41Ter) was identified in the patient and her mother, and Danon disease was diagnosed."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand (no tables); JSON assembled with a short Python script, every value from my reading. In scope: the proband ('patient', rule 5; the paper calls her 'the patient'), her mother (LAMP2 carrier), and two relatives described in relation to her: the brother (affected: HCM, arrhythmias, died after cardiac transplant; never stated as tested) and the father (arrhythmias; tested, carries the KCNE1 variant; his LAMP2 status is not stated). KCNE1 variant recorded for the patient and father because the paper attributes it to both explicitly. LAMP2 inheritance for the patient recorded as inherited maternal because the paper states the mother carries the same variant. Zygosity not stated for anyone. Author wording 'novel nonsense mutation'/'previously unreported' not taken as a pathogenicity class. Age at diagnosis of Danon disease is not printed as an age (diagnosed after AF 'Eleven years later' than presentation at 21), so left not reported; onset ISO left null because 'Eleven years later' is a time after presentation, not an age. Checklist LVH for the brother marked observed from 'hypertrophic cardiomyopathy'. Arrhythmias in mother/father/brother are unspecified, so no arrhythmia checklist item marked. Possible inconsistency: Figure 6 legend says the mother's initial fundus photograph 'shows intact macular area' while the Discussion reports 'minor annular hypopigmentary alterations in the macula' at the initial visit; 'macular involvement' excluded for the mother is taken from the 12-year image ('sparing the macular area'), and the macular alterations recorded as observed. Abstract gives the variant also as 'c.123 of exon 2'; the full string from the Case Report was used. ERG 'modest decrease in the rod response' recorded observed with detail 'remained within the normal range'.
